title: short-rate-anomaly-regimes: replication and monetary-regime extension of short-rate asset-pricing anomaly models
description:
Research compendium for the paper Short Term Interest Rate Innovations Across Monetary Regimes. The repository reconstructs and extends the two-factor ICAPM of Maio and Santa-Clara (2017, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 52(3), 927-961, DOI 10.1017/S002210901700028X), in which the pricing factors are the market excess return and the innovation in a short-term interest rate.

The compendium provides: immutable acquisition of public inputs with raw and normalized checksums, retrieval timestamps, vintage labels, and redistribution status; a verified audit of the monthly aggregation of the federal funds and three-month Treasury-bill rate series against their daily counterparts; AR(1) short-rate innovation reconstruction with an automatically tested timing convention; publication-era and current vintages of the Kenneth French, Hou-Xue-Zhang q-factor, and Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity files together with a revision comparison; per-family availability records for the seven anomaly decile portfolio families; and an immutable, validated canonical monthly panel for 1972-01 to 2013-12.

The design separates exact replication from documented reconstruction and never labels a reconstruction as replication. No input in the current release qualifies as exact, because the article names data providers and people rather than files; every derived analysis therefore carries a documented-reconstruction label. Replication readiness, per-target classifications, and the remaining blocking inputs are recorded in reports/baseline_input_readiness.md.

No raw data, licensed database extracts, or restricted author-provided files are redistributed. Acquisition scripts reproduce every public input from its source.

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: School of Media Arts and Design, Polytechnic of Porto, Portugal

notes: Public data sources used and separately licensed by their providers: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) at the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; the Kenneth R. French Data Library; the Hou, Xue, and Zhang q-factor library at global-q.org; and the Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity series published by Robert F. Stambaugh. Publication-era vintages were retrieved from the Internet Archive. This repository redistributes none of those files; it distributes the acquisition code, checksums, and provenance manifests needed to obtain and verify them.
